problem: Consolidate heterogeneous robot datasets and test when cross-embodiment co-training improves existing robot-policy performance.
contribution: Open X-Embodiment standardizes a large multi-institution dataset repository and studies RT-1-X/RT-2-X models trained on a subset of its embodiments.
algorithm: Consolidate observation/action formats, choose a canonical camera and normalize each dataset's end-effector controls. Train RT-1-X with robot data or co-finetune RT-2-X with robot/web examples. Evaluate transfer/scale/history/data-source ablations.
observations: Image history and task language, with camera placement varying by dataset. Common serialization does not align all scene or robot coordinate frames.
actions: Coarsely aligned7Dend-effector/gripper variables plus termination. Absolute positions, deltas and velocities retain source-specific meanings; denormalization depends on embodiment, so identical vectors can induce different physical motion.
embodiment_and_data: Paper describes60datasets across22embodiments/21institutions and527skills. Actual model training mixture covers9embodiments available at experiment time, rather than all22listed in the evolving dataset.
experiments: 3600evaluation trials across six robots in the reported study; known-embodiment co-training and transferred task concepts, model-capacity/history and removal-of-Bridge ablations. This is not an unseen-robot zero-shot control qualification.
baselines: Original local methods, RT-1, RT-1-X and RT-2/RT-2-X with differing capacity/web training. Published overall positive-transfer aggregates coexist with negative per-setting results.

quantitative_result.value: High-data TableI: Google RT-1paper6skills RT-192% versusRT-1-X73%; Stanford Bridge RT-140% versusRT-1-X27%. RT-2-X55B scores91% and50%respectively. Thus co-training is not uniformly beneficial, especially under capacity limits.

limitations: Action units/frames/control frequencies remain heterogeneous; small models underfit large mixtures. Paper explicitly leaves generalization to new robots and criteria for positive transfer as open problems. Dataset count and actual training mixture must not be conflated.
code_and_license: Primary dataset/model design examined; individual source-dataset rights and current tooling revisions require separate audits. No aggregate license can be assumed to grant every component/model right; no RT-X execution is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Reuse per-dataset schema, normalization, camera and robot identity provenance. Do not transfer a common7Dvector directly to SO101/ROSMASTER or assume inclusion in a data family makes an unseen robot compatible.
